chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who has sores and injuries and experiences sexual impurity. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with him not performing ghusl and performing tayammum.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person with sores or injuries who needs to perform ghusl for janabah?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that a person with wounds or sores who becomes junub is not required to perform the full ritual bath (ghusl) if it causes harm, but may instead perform tayammum. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'la darar' (no harm), prioritizing ease in ritual purity when physical conditions prevent water usage. The hadith underscores the flexibility of fiqh in accommodating medical realities without compromising spiritual obligations.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the man who happens to be with the sores and the injuries, experiences the sexual impurity. Heasws said: ‘There is no problem with it if he does not wash, and he performs Tayammum’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “

I once asked Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man on whose body there are dimples or wounds and experiences sexual relation. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful if one does not take Ghusl (bath) in such condition, instead takes Tayammum.’’’
